overview: Knee joint replaced with an implant due to severe arthritis/injury.
duration: Full recovery often 3–6 months (strength/function continue to improve to 6months).
physio_importance: Reduce pain, regain knee ROM & strength, restore walking and daily activities.
modalities: No modalities (exercise focused )

overview: Damaged hip joint replaced (arthritis / fracture).
duration: Full recovery 3–6 months (functional gains earlier, strength continues to improve).
physio_importance: Restore walking, balance, strength; prevent limp and complications.
modalities: No modalities (exercise focused)

overview: Tear of knee stabilizing ligament; often repaired surgically.
duration: 6-9 months to return to sport; daily activities improve earlier (1–3 months).
physio_importance: Restore stability, strength, neuromuscular control to avoid re-injury.
modalities: Strengthening, balance, functional training; modalities for pain (ULTRASOUND/TENS - IF IT IS NOT OPERATATED)

overview: Tear of shoulder tendons; surgery for larger tears.
duration: 3-6 months typical for recovery after repair.
physio_importance: Protect repair, restore ROM, then rebuild shoulder strength and overhead function.
modalities: Early: protection/pain control (ice); later: therapeutic exercise; manual therapy, Modalities (MS - IF IT IS NOT OPERATED)

overview: Any shoulder surgery to fix rotator cuff, labrum, etc.
duration: 3–6 months for most to return to full function (varies).
physio_importance: Restore motion, strength, scapular control, reduce pain.
modalities: Exercise, manual therapy, pain control (ice/TENS)

overview: Broken bone — rehab starts after bone is stable/healed.
duration: Upper limb ~6–8 weeks; lower limb ~8–12 weeks (complex longer).
physio_importance: Restore joint ROM, strength, return to function and safe loading.
modalities: ROM, progressive strengthening, gait retraining

overview: Operations on lumbar/cervical spine (discectomy, fusion etc.).
duration: 4–6 months common; complex cases may need longer and staged rehab.
physio_importance: Rebuild core strength, mobility, protect spine, restore function.
modalities: Exercise, neural mobilization, graded activity; modalities for pain as needed

overview: Heel pain from overuse/strain of plantar fascia.
duration: 4–8 weeks typical with good treatment; chronic can take months.
physio_importance: Stretching, load management, strengthening and footwear advice to stop recurrence.
modalities: Taping, orthotics, night splints, shockwave (for chronic), exercise

overview: Tendon pain from overload/degeneration.
duration: 6–12 weeks for many; chronic cases may take 3–6 months.
physio_importance: Gradual load-progression, eccentric loading, restore tendon tolerance.
modalities: Exercise therapy (high-load eccentrics), shockwave for chronic, taping

overview: Pain in lumbar area; acute to chronic forms.
duration: Acute: 2–4 weeks improvement; subacute/chronic: 6–12+ weeks or more.
physio_importance: Reduce pain, improve movement control, strengthen core, prevent recurrence.
modalities: Exercise, education, manual therapy, TENS/heat for symptom relief

overview: Wear & tear of joint cartilage causing pain/stiffness.
duration: 8–12 weeks supervised physio for meaningful improvement; maintenance ongoing.
physio_importance: Strengthen muscles around joint, improve mobility and reduce pain long-term.
modalities: Exercise, education, walking program; TENS/heat for pain relief; orthotics

overview: Pain in cervical spine; acute or chronic.
duration: Acute: 2–4 weeks; chronic: 6–12+ weeks depending on cause.
physio_importance: Restore motion, reduce pain, strengthen postural muscles, ergonomic education.
modalities: Exercise, manual therapy, heat/TENS for pain relief

overview: Progressive shoulder stiffness & pain.
duration: Total course often 9 months–2 years; active physio over many months (≈3–12+ months).
physio_importance: Relieve pain, maintain motion, gradual stretching & mobilization to thaw joint.
modalities: Manual therapy/joint mobilization, exercises; modalities for pain control

overview: Progressive neurological condition causing movement slowness & balance issues.
duration: Rehab is ongoing; blocks of intensive physio (e.g. 8–12 weeks) help function; lifelong maintenance.
physio_importance: Improve gait, balance, transfers, reduce fall risk and maintain independence.
modalities: Gait training, balance exercises, cueing, task training; modalities rarely primary

overview: Rehab after childbirth (pelvic floor, core, posture).
duration: 4–12 weeks initial program; may continue longer for pelvic floor issues.
physio_importance: Restore pelvic floor function, core strength, posture, and reduce pain.
modalities: Pelvic floor training, core exercises; biofeedback as needed

overview: Antenatal care for pain, posture and pelvic floor.
duration: Short programs during pregnancy (weeks-months) as needed; symptom-based.
physio_importance: Reduce back/pelvic pain, teach safe exercise and prepare pelvic floor.
modalities: Exercise, posture advice, manual therapy, education

overview: Recovery after brain stroke affecting movement/speech.
duration: Major gains 3–6 months; rehab often continues 6–12+ months and sometimes lifelong.
physio_importance: Restore mobility, strength, balance, ADLs; neuro-retraining is key.
modalities: Neuro-rehab exercises, gait training, task-specific training, electrical stimulation

overview: Progressive muscle weakness disorders (chronic).
duration: Lifelong physiotherapy to maintain function; no cure.
physio_importance: Maintain mobility, slow loss of function, prevent contractures.
modalities: Stretching, strengthening (as tolerated), positioning

overview: Neurological disease with relapses & progression.
duration: Rehab ongoing; short courses (e.g. 6–12 weeks) improve function; maintenance long-term.
physio_importance: Improve mobility, reduce fatigue, maintain strength, adapt activities.
modalities: Exercise programs, balance training, energy-conservation strategies

overview: Nerve injury at birth causing arm weakness.
duration: Weeks to months for mild cases; severe may need surgery and longer rehab (months–years).
physio_importance: Improve movement, prevent contractures, stimulate muscle activation.
modalities: Neuro-developmental therapy, passive/active exercises

overview: Median nerve compression at wrist causing hand numbness/weakness.
duration: Weeks to months with conservative care; post-op rehab 4–8 weeks.
physio_importance: Reduce nerve irritation, improve hand function, strengthen/wrist mechanics.
modalities: Nerve gliding, exercises, ice; post-op scar & nerve mobilization

overview: Non-progressive brain injury causing lifelong motor impairment.
duration: Lifelong physiotherapy with periodic intensive blocks depending on goals.
physio_importance: Improve mobility, prevent contractures, train function and adaptive strategies.
modalities: Stretching, strengthening, gait training, positioning

overview: Facial nerve weakness causing drooping of one side of face.
duration: Many recover in weeks–months; majority within 3–6 months.
physio_importance: Facial retraining, massage, neuromuscular facilitation to restore symmetry.
modalities: Facial exercises, neuromuscular re-education; electrical stimulation sometimes used

overview: Ligament stretch/tear around ankle from twisting injury.
duration: Mild: 1–3 weeks; moderate: 4–6 weeks; severe: >6–12 weeks.
physio_importance: Reduce pain/swelling, restore ROM, strength, proprioception to avoid re-injury.
modalities: RICE initially, balance training, strengthening; tape as needed
